clue.text: Curse a plot to ruin the gambling man

indicators.note: ruining these words wrecks their order, so the letters are scrambled into a new word

explanation.surface: Someone casts a spell intended to bring down a gambler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ruin' says the ten letters of CURSE A PLOT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A speculator takes risky financial bets in hope of profit, a gambler of the markets.

clue.text: Rifle fire

explanation.definitionFit: To loot a captured town is to plunder it, and dismissing an employee is giving them the push.

clue.text: Watches a series that's distressing for the viewers

parts.note: eyes as a verb means watches
a train is a succession or series, as in a train of events

explanation.surface: Someone sees a TV series that upsets the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewers' suggests the audience, but means the eyes themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatigue from overusing the eyes is a strain on them, troubling to those organs of sight.

clue.text: In default, rascals are totally unrestrained

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the run of letters in these words

explanation.surface: When they fail to pay up, the rogues are utterly wild.
explanation.definitionFit: An extremist, going beyond the usual bounds, is extreme and unlimited.

clue.text: Appearing eccentric is inane-really senseless

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are put into a strange order

explanation.surface: Looking odd is daft, truly pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges IS INANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means as silly as a donkey, utterly foolish.

clue.text: Duck ranks as fruit!

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, the letter O
ranges are rows or ranks, as of hills

explanation.surface: A duck lines up as a fruit!
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of nothing in cricket, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Citrus fruits of the colour named after them.

clue.text: Top people who are for staying outside of the church

indicators.note: one word staying outside another wraps round it, so the church abbreviation sits inside

parts.note: for can mean as, in the sense of acting in a role (as captain / for captain)
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Elite figures who support keeping out of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staying outside of' puts AS (for) round CE, the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Experts at the very top of their field are called aces, as with fighter pilots.

clue.text: Boat-building know-how

explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is a sailing vessel, and manual skill is the know-how of the artisan.

clue.text: A good man indisposed to go about and another causing a stoppage

indicators.note: one piece goes about the other, surrounding it

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man
ill means unwell
taken as written
a second saint, ST again

explanation.surface: A kind person feeling unwell wanders around with a companion, bringing things to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go about' puts AND ST inside ST + ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete halt, where nothing moves, is a full stop.

clue.text: The depressed area?

parts.note: sounds like a deprived region but plays on down meaning low or sad; in fact refers to rolling chalk hills

explanation.walkthrough: Downs are rounded grassy hills in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Gently rolling open chalk hills are called downs, and their stretch of country takes the name.

clue.text: An expanding case?

parts.note: suggests luggage that stretches, but means the part of the body that swells as you breathe in, also a word for a storage box

explanation.definitionFit: The thorax rises and swells with each breath, and a large lidded box shares its name.

clue.text: One loved raising Italian capital at a Roman retreat

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its opening letter, here of Italian
to retreat is to go backwards, so these words are read in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone dear sets up an Italian capital at a Roman hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' puts the I (Italian's capital) on top; 'retreat' turns AT A ROMAN into NAMORATA.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a female sweetheart or lover, from the Italian for being in love.

clue.text: Taking fish after tea's quite wrong

indicators.note: the fish comes after the scrambled tea letters
letters that are quite wrong are out of order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of tea's, the apostrophe dropped
ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Grabbing fish after teatime is bad behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite wrong' rearranges TEAS into STEA; 'after' puts LING behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is the dishonest carrying off of what belongs to another, a kind of seizing.

clue.text: Made a record like a celebrity

explanation.surface: Someone recorded a song in the manner of a star.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing something down means jotting it, and a famous person is called eminent or renowned in the same word.

clue.text: A city or county to be seen in inclement weather

indicators.note: the county is to be seen inside the weather word

parts.note: winter is the season of harsh weather
Ches is the abbreviation for Cheshire, an English county

explanation.surface: A town or shire visible in a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be seen in' puts CHES (Cheshire) inside WINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Winchester is a cathedral city in Hampshire, once England's capital.

clue.text: Fancy a copy to go around in

indicators.note: one piece goes around another, so the second sits inside the first

parts.note: an image is a likeness or copy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Picture a duplicate wrapping round something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go around' puts IN inside IMAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy, as in 'fancy that!', is to picture something in the mind.

clue.text: An impractical individual is thought to heel over

parts.note: an idea is a thought
a ship lists when it heels or leans over

explanation.surface: A dreamer's notion is to lean right over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heel' suggests a foot, but means a ship tilting.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamer pursuing perfection rather than practicality is a visionary.

clue.text: This plant report includes absolutely everything

indicators.note: one word includes another by holding it inside

parts.note: a report is the bang of a gun, a shot
all means everything without exception

explanation.surface: A news report on a factory covers everything about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' suggests news, but it is the noise of a gun; 'includes' puts ALL inside SHOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mild onion is grown as a garden vegetable, a bulb plant.

clue.text: The key worker Mick's loth to replace

indicators.note: replacing the letters puts them in new positions, a rearrangement

parts.note: Mick's with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: An essential worker whom Mick is unwilling to find a substitute for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' rearranges MICKS LOTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who makes and repairs locks and keys.

clue.text: Satisfied constituents

definitions.meaning: happy with things as they are
the things contained, the substance of something

explanation.definitionFit: Pleased and happy is one sense; stressed on the first syllable it means the ingredients inside.

clue.text: Facing the world

parts.note: suggests confronting life bravely, but means the layer that forms the face or surface of the earth

explanation.definitionFit: The uppermost layer of earth is the surface covering the ground.

clue.text: Concerned with healing, it may be claimed

indicators.note: says the word that follows could be another word once its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A claim that something helps with curing illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it may be' signals rearranging CLAIMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicine is the science of curing illness, and its adjective describes doctors' work.

clue.text: A man of music may well exercise some art

indicators.note: exercising the letters works them about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A musician might practise some artistry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercise' rearranges SOME ART.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinguished conductor or composer is given this Italian title.

clue.text: Bearing on the water-supply in town

parts.note: E, east, is a compass bearing
a well supplies water from underground

explanation.surface: A direction given about the local water source in a town.
explanation.walkthrough: EWELL is a town in Surrey, south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewell is a town in Surrey near Epsom.

clue.text: Uplifting Oriental tale giving delight

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting letters up reads them from bottom to top, in reverse

parts.note: E for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: An inspiring story from the East that brings joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplifting' turns E + TALE upwards, ETALE read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate is to make someone joyful, to thrill them.

clue.text: Lacking nobility?

parts.note: read literally, being without lords and dukes; in fact the word means unrivalled, having no equal

explanation.definitionFit: Something without equals is unmatched; peers are both nobles and equals.

clue.text: Go the French way

parts.note: le is French for the
Ave is short for avenue, a road or way

explanation.surface: Head off in the Gallic manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart is to go away.

clue.text: A drop of drink, right?

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: Just a little of a beverage, correct?
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop' suggests a small drink; it is a drop from the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A single drop of liquid from the eye when crying.

clue.text: Cars to electrify

definitions.meaning: vehicles, a means of getting around
to thrill, carry away with emotion

explanation.definitionFit: Vehicles are a means of conveyance, and to enrapture someone is to carry them away with delight.

clue.text: Lively, though the time is about 1-50

indicators.note: one word is about another when it surrounds it

parts.note: an age is a period or era of time
Roman numerals: I is one, L is fifty

explanation.surface: Sprightly, although it's nearly ten to two.
explanation.walkthrough: '1-50' looks like a clock time, but gives Roman I and L; 'is about' puts them inside AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone nimble and quick on their feet is spry and lively.

clue.text: Unacceptable sound that's deplored

indicators.note: the word is to be heard as speech, giving one with the same pronunciation

parts.note: rude behaviour is impolite and unacceptable

explanation.surface: A noise considered offensive and regretted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' signals that RUDE (unacceptable) is said aloud, giving its twin.
explanation.definitionFit: Regretted bitterly; to rue something is to lament it.

clue.text: Health-centre to impress the woman in general

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters

parts.note: taken as written
to get someone is to strike or affect them strongly
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A clinic sets out to win over a female patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes AL from the middle of HEALTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken as a whole or on the whole means overall, broadly speaking.
